143.title: Be Curious · Which Doesn’t Belong?
steps: Notice which expressions repeat the same number.
Choose one expression that is different.
Explain your reason; another person may have a different valid reason.
143.answer: One possible answer: 6 × 8, because it is not a square fact. Other choices are possible with a defensible explanation.
143.hint: Look at all four multiplication expressions.

144.title: Patterns in the table
steps: Compare 10 and 100, then 100 and 1,000.

146.title: 16 · Jenny’s choice
steps: Her father gives $10.
Grandfather offers 10 times that amount.
Compare 10 times the grandfather’s offer with $500.
146.answer: Grandfather: $100. Ten times $100 is $1,000, which is greater than $500. Choose the $1,000 offer.
146.hint: Work out the offers one person at a time.
146.verification: Original source visually checked; independently evaluated; no official answer key in supplied PDF.

146.title: 17 · Inequality
steps: Evaluate four factors of 10.
Evaluate 10⁶.
Choose a number strictly between those values.
146.answer: Any number strictly between 10,000 and 1,000,000 works, such as 100,000. The textbook inequality does not specify a unique b.
146.hint: Find the lower and upper bounds.

146.title: Reflect · Patterns
steps: Write 10², 10³, and 10⁴.
Count the zeros after the 1.
Describe the connection.
146.answer: For a whole-number exponent n greater than zero, 10ⁿ is 1 followed by n zeros.
146.hint: Think about the number of zeros in powers of 10.
